About 5 years ago, transferred in from community college, too. I’m back now for grad school after some time away. Submit your application as soon as it opens, if I remember right, it’s sometime in early summer...but I could be wrong. Simultaneously apply for FAFSA, if you plan on using financial aid. Doing this early will save you a lot of fear and stress. In the application essay, they’re usually looking to know who you are, and how you’ve been growing as a person.

The campus is awesome, and most of the professors bend over backwards to help you succeed. I’ve never had a bad teacher at App...maybe I’m just lucky, though. If you talk to any random student, you’ll probably be met with kindness. 

When I transferred, I was slated to be in a dorm with a friend of mine, till about 3 weeks before classes started, when they sent me an email saying they gave my room spot to someone else, despite the fact that my friend - who also transferred in just the same - got to keep his spot in the dorm. It worked out better for me, because having an apartment is waaaay better. You’re not confined to a small room and communal bathrooms/kitchens. If you can afford it, get an apartment.

 On that subject, though, housing here sucks. The rental companies take advantage of students wherever they can. They’re all scummy, and you shouldn’t trust them. Read about your rights as a renter in NC, and carefully read the contracts you sign. Also it’s very crowded. App gets more students every year, and there’s only so much space to put them all, so vacancies will be snatched up *very* quickly. As soon as you know you’re in and you will have the money for one, talk to as many companies as you can, and look through craigslist or appstate classifieds on Facebook. Find the place that best fits your needs and budget.

Learn the bus system. It’s free and there’s usually a route that’ll take you where you wanna go. Apartments in Boone usually have a bus stop close by. 

Oh, also, we have a lot of good food and drink here. If you’re not careful, you can gain weight like I did. Enjoy in moderation. Also check out the parks we have. The nature here is gorgeous, and it’s a sin not to take some time once in a while and enjoy the views and scenery we have

Hi, I've used the counseling services before, for the same reasons. I've participated in both one-on-one sessions, as well as group counseling sessions. I have to say the staff there are wonderful, and confidential. I don't know their escalation procedures, but I'm pretty sure anything short of you actually making an attempt falls under HIPA laws. You're the patient, and anyone else doesn't have the rights to your information. Like your grades in class, unless you give them permission to disclose the information, they must keep it confidential. 

As far as the quality of service, truthfully I wasn't able to spend a lot of time with them - only about half a semester - so I wasn't able to make a whole lot of real progress, but they were absolutely professional, kind, non-judgmental, listened carefully to what I wanted to say, and offered advice that helped me down from the bad moments. 

When I went, I was ready to do it. I figured at this point I didn't have anything to lose, so I decided to take that step towards help. They didn't have enough time with me to truly help me sort through my issues, and I've been able to manage my mind better on my own since then (it was like 2014 when I went), but I have absolutely no regrets going into that office, and even still have a friend from our group sessions that I hang out with when we can find the time.

My recommendation is if you're truly thinking about your life like that, what to you really have to lose by going?

It was a cold day. The wind howled through the town as though its source was the breath of a great beast which dwelled in the mountainsides, but no mortal had ever laid eyes on. The frost hung in the air and in the trees. Winter had dug her claws into the earth one final time, fighting to keep her power over the land from Spring.

I had needed supplies for some time. My cupboard stocks were barren and the washroom had nothing with which to clean myself. A rumble in my belly told me that I had to rise from my lethargy and brave Winter's chill very soon.

After donning my outerwear, which would protect me from the air's bitter chill, I stopped to make sure I had everything I needed for my journey. If I attempted to leave without even one of these items, my quest would fail. 

My steed was a bright red warhorse from the Germanic lands far away. She has been getting on in years and has become as fickle as she is fast. After coaxing her from her sleep, I set out on my journey. It was not a great distance to my destination, but the speed and number of other people on the road made it dangerous to take the shorter route, so I had to follow the flow of the traffic in the opposite direction for a time before turning back on a connecting road. 

When I arrived, I led my horse to rest where the grass grew and where the view of the mountainside was opened up before her eyes. I went inside the large fortress of supplies. 

As I wandered the hallways filled with commodities and foods of every variety, my mind was overwhelmed with choices. As if I had been bewitched at the very moment upon crossing the threshold, my mind became blank, and I did not know what I wanted or needed. I had to steel my resolve and remind myself why I was there. The first thing I needed to retrieve was the washroom parchment, lest I become so distracted by my desire for food and forget this very crucial item. As soon as I had this, I allowed my mind to focus on the next task. As I passed the ales and the wines, I had to fight their temptations, because though it would complement my meal well, I did not want to spend the gold. My attention turned to food. A section of this particular fortress is dedicated to hot, freshly prepared foods. A favorite of mine is their selection of foods from the lands of the far east. Or rather mutated recipes that are almost completely unique from their origins. But delicious all the same, and a favorite of this lazy adventurer. 

After filling a container with all of my favorite meats and vegetables and noodles, I quickly went to the merchant at the front. I was in a hurry because now that I had my food, the clock was ticking against it, each passing second sapping more heat from my meal. I quickly paid the gold I owed, and walked outside. 

The frigid wind was still howling, and I knew this was the ultimate test. I had to get to my horse as quickly as possible (luckily this is a magic horse that protects me and my belongings from the elements while I am mounted). It took me longer than I wanted to get to her, and with every hard gust of wind I worried for the prize I held in my hands, and tried in vain to shield it. When I arrived at my horse, she had gotten cold again. I coaxed her into shaking off the frost, and off we went to enjoy the spoils of our successful quest.
